sources: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: JWT attacks (algorithm handling of unsigned tokens) - https://portswigger.net/web-security/jwt
Python re module: $ also matches before a trailing newline - https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html

defects.description: verify_token reads alg from the unverified header and looks it up in _DIGESTS; for any alg outside the table (for example a header naming no signing algorithm) the digest is None, the if-block that compares the signature is skipped, and the payload is returned as a valid session whatever the signature segment contains. Spec R1 requires HS256 only and a signature check before the payload is trusted.

USERNAME_PATTERN is anchored with ^ and $ and used with .match(); $ matches before a trailing newline, so the input 'admin' followed by a line feed passes validate_username and is returned unchanged as 'admin\n'. It is a distinct string from 'admin' (uniqueness checks on the stored name are bypassed), and accounts.py audit_line writes it into the audit entry, which splits the entry across two lines. Spec R2 forbids line breaks.

account_from_request builds the Account from the whole request payload via Account(**{**payload, ...}); a request body containing is_admin true (with valid username, display_name and role) yields Account(is_admin=True). Spec R3 allows only username, display_name and role from the client.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: hmac.compare_digest is used for the signature comparison, which is constant time (spec R4). The digest is computed from the exact header and payload segments, so this check is correct when a digest is selected.
secrets.token_urlsafe(16) is a CSPRNG token used as a unique token id (jti); it is not used for prediction-resistant keys and is unchanged from the base.
random.uniform is used only for retry back-off jitter, which is not a security-relevant value; no secret, token or code is derived from it.

Unchanged line in verify_reset_code: the reset code is compared with == instead of hmac.compare_digest, which is a real flaw against spec R4. It is not on a line the change added or changed, so a diff-mode reviewer must not report it; it is listed here only as a preexisting flaw.
